# kappanhang

**Opens an Icom network radio as an ordinary sound card and serial port**

- **Version recorded:** 1.3
- **Categories:** `rig-control`, `station`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/nonoo/kappanhang>

## What it does

Connects to a network-capable Icom transceiver over its own IP protocol and presents the radio's audio as a PulseAudio device and its serial stream as a virtual serial port on your machine. Programs then use the remote radio exactly as if it were plugged in.

## Why you would want it

It makes remote operating transparent to everything else. Rather than each program needing to understand Icom's network protocol, fldigi, WSJT-X and a logger see a sound card and a serial port, and none of them has to know the radio is elsewhere. That is a much better shape than per-application remote support.

## Before it will work

A network-capable Icom radio -- IC-705, IC-7610, IC-9700 and similar -- with its network settings enabled and a user and password configured on the radio. A route to it.

## How it installs

- apt: `kappanhang`

## Known problems

Audio over an unreliable link produces dropouts that look like propagation, which matters when you are judging a weak signal. Only one client can hold the radio's network session at a time, so this and wfview cannot both be connected. The radio's own credentials are the only authentication between a network and your transmitter; treat exposing it as the decision it is.
